dataset.name: WHONDRS Surface Water Dissolved Organic Carbon and FTICR-MS across Glacial Features in Svalbard 2022
description: This dataset supports a broader study examining climatic forcing of terrestrial greenhouse gas emission through permafrost and glaciers in Svalbard. The dataset provides geochemistry and organic matter characterization data generated from surface water collected from 11 sites across central Svalbard. Data were also collected in 2021 and can be found at https://data.ess-dive.lbl.gov/view/doi:10.15485/1888571. Additional related data were collected and will be published separately in collaboration with Yde and Kleber.

This dataset is comprised of one main data folder containing (1) file-level metadata; (2) data dictionary; (3) field metadata; (4) dissolved organic carbon (DOC; measured as non-purgeable organic carbon; NPOC); (5) surface water sampling protocol; (6) readme; (7) methods codes; (8) international geo-sample number (IGSN) mapping file; (9) a folder of field photos; and (10) folder of high resolution characterization of organic matter via 7 Tesla Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FTICR-MS) generated through the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory (EMSL; https://www.pnnl.gov/environmental-molecular-sciences-laboratory). The FTICR folder contains two subfolders, one containing the .xml data files and the other containing instructions for using Formularity (https://omics.pnl.gov/software/formularity) and an R script to process the data based on the user's specific needs. All files are .csv, .pdf, .R, .ref, or .xml.

measurementTechnique: Samples were collected across central Svalbard in 2022. Site metadata, including general environmental information, were manually recorded in the field. See WHONDRS_YDE22_Sampling_Protocol.pdf for details on sample and site metadata collection. Surface water samples were syringe-filtered into pre-acidified vials in the field and refrigerated until ready for laboratory processing that included solid phase extraction (SPE) before FTICR-MS analysis. Samples were shipped internationally on blue ice, but shipping time exceeded the lifespan of the ice. Upon receipt, they were refrigerated and analyzed for NPOC and FTICR-MS. For details regarding laboratory and instrument methods, see the alphanumeric methods codes located in the header rows of the chemistry data csv file and their associated definitions in YDE22_Methods_Codes.csv. Data formats follow ESS-DIVE Reporting Formats.
